subject: economy
note: Original notes following NCERT economics 9–12 (there is no separate 6–8 economics book; those years sit inside geography ‘resources’ and social science). Class 11–12 cover Indian Economic Development, Statistics (light), Micro and Macro.

chapters.title: The Story of Village Palampur
chapters.summary: A model village to teach factors of production: land, labour, physical capital, human capital. Multiple cropping, HYV, small vs large farmers, and non-farm work (dairy, transport, shop). Modern farming needs cheap working capital—often debt.

chapters.title: People as Resource
chapters.summary: Population becomes human capital through education and health. Unemployment (seasonal, disguised, educated) wastes that capital. Women’s work is undercounted. Investment in people raises productivity.

chapters.title: Poverty as a Challenge
chapters.summary: Poverty as capability failure, not only income. Estimates, social groups, interstate variation. Causes: colonial drain, low growth earlier, inequality, social exclusion. Anti-poverty: growth + targeted schemes (historical MGNREGA-type idea).

chapters.title: Food Security in India
chapters.summary: Availability, access, absorption. Buffer stocks, PDS, cooperatives. Hunger can exist with granaries if access fails. Revise NFSA in current affairs on top of this chapter.

chapters.title: Development
chapters.summary: Different people, different development goals. Income vs HDI (health, education). Sustainability: groundwater, environment. National development is comparison plus justice, not only average income.

chapters.title: Sectors of the Indian Economy
chapters.summary: Primary, secondary, tertiary; organised vs unorganised; public vs private. Tertiary’s rising share vs still-large farm employment—structural change is incomplete. MGNREGA and labour protection appear as policy.

chapters.title: Money and Credit
chapters.summary: Money as medium of exchange, modern forms, banks, cheques, formal vs informal credit. Cheap formal credit is development; informal high-interest credit traps the poor. RBI oversees banks.

chapters.title: Globalisation and the Indian Economy
chapters.summary: MNCs, trade liberalisation, WTO, SEZs, winners and losers among producers and workers. Globalisation is technology + policy, not fate. Connect to 1991 reforms at plus-two.

chapters.title: Consumer Rights
chapters.summary: COPRA, consumer forums, rights to safety, information, choice, redressal. Markets need rules. ISI/Agmark as quality marks.

chapters.title: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
chapters.summary: Stagnant agriculture, deindustrialisation, poor infrastructure, drain, low literacy. The colonial structure is the starting point of planning.

chapters.title: Indian Economy 1950–1990
chapters.summary: Planning Commission, mixed economy, land reforms, Green Revolution, industry (IPR 1956), public sector. Achievements and the licence-permit costs. Food self-sufficiency vs inefficiency debate.

chapters.title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation
chapters.summary: 1991 crisis, LPG, WTO era, NITI replacing Planning Commission in later current affairs. Outcomes: growth, inequality, services boom, farm distress unfinished.

chapters.title: Poverty
chapters.summary: Measurement debates, causes, policy (growth vs targeted), multidimensional poverty in later data. Link Class 9 to technical estimates.

chapters.title: Human Capital Formation
chapters.summary: Education and health as investment. India’s education structure, still-large quality gaps, gender. Human capital vs human development.

chapters.title: Rural Development
chapters.summary: Credit (cooperatives, SHGs, NABARD), agriculture marketing, organic farming, diversification (animal husbandry, fisheries). Rural is not only crop.

chapters.title: Employment: Growth, Informalisation
chapters.summary: Workforce, self vs hired, informalisation, jobless growth worry, government as employer. Quality of jobs matters as much as count.

chapters.title: Infrastructure
chapters.summary: Energy, transport, communication, health, education as infrastructure. Public–private mix, energy shortages, health as right vs commodity.

chapters.title: Environment and Sustainable Development
chapters.summary: Carrying capacity, pollution, Chipko to contemporary climate. Development that keeps future options open. India’s dual burden: poverty and pollution.

chapters.title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Neighbours
chapters.summary: India, Pakistan, China: growth paths, demographic transition, HDI, reforms timing. China is not a photocopyable model; institutions differ.

chapters.title: Introduction & Collection of Data
chapters.summary: Why statistics, primary vs secondary data, census vs sample, NSSO/NSO as sources. Bad data makes bad policy.

chapters.title: Organisation and Presentation of Data
chapters.summary: Variables, frequency, tables, bar, pie, histogram. Presentation is argument.

chapters.title: Measures of Central Tendency & Dispersion
chapters.summary: Mean, median, mode; range, quartile deviation, mean deviation, SD, Lorenz curve / Gini flavour. Averages hide inequality.

chapters.title: Correlation & Index Numbers
chapters.summary: Correlation is not causation. CPI, WPI, GDP deflator as index numbers for inflation. Base year matters.

chapters.title: National Income Accounting
chapters.summary: GDP, GNP, NNP, factor cost vs market price, real vs nominal, value added. What GDP misses (home work, environment).

chapters.title: Money and Banking
chapters.summary: Functions of money, money supply measures, credit creation, RBI instruments (repo, CRR, SLR, OMOs). Monetary policy vs inflation targeting in current affairs.

chapters.title: Determination of Income and Employment
chapters.summary: Keynesian idea: output can be demand-constrained. Consumption, savings, investment, multiplier. Simple AD–AS story without drowning in graphs.

chapters.title: Government Budget and the Economy
chapters.summary: Revenue vs capital, deficits (fiscal, revenue, primary), FRBM idea, subsidies, tax vs non-tax. Budget is GS-III every year.

chapters.title: Open Economy — Macroeconomics
chapters.summary: BoP, current vs capital account, exchange rates (flexible, fixed, managed), CAD. Link to RBI and trade policy.

chapters.title: Introduction (Micro)
chapters.summary: Central problems: what, how, for whom. PPC, opportunity cost, positive vs normative. Micro is the household and firm; macro is the aggregate.

chapters.title: Theory of Consumer Behaviour
chapters.summary: Utility, indifference (idea), demand curve, elasticity. Why demand slopes down.

chapters.title: Production and Costs
chapters.summary: Short run vs long run, TP–AP–MP, cost curves (idea). Production needs time to adjust capital.

chapters.title: The Theory of the Firm & Perfect Competition
chapters.summary: Revenue, profit maximisation idea, features of perfect competition. Real markets are imperfect—use this as a benchmark.

chapters.title: Market Equilibrium & Imperfect markets (overview)
chapters.summary: Demand–supply equilibrium, price ceiling/floor (MSP as a floor flavour), monopoly/oligopoly as real GS examples (digital markets, telecom).

chapters.title: Non-competitive Markets (idea)
chapters.summary: Monopoly, monopolistic competition, oligopoly. Why regulators (CCI, TRAI) exist. Link to GS-II/III regulation.
